title: MCP DB-Server SQL Abuse -- SSRF to Internal / Cloud-Metadata Target via DuckDB httpfs (T1552.005)
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin canonical templates
description:
Detects server-side request forgery (SSRF) through an MCP database server that passes SQL straight to a DuckDB engine. DuckDB ships the httpfs extension; "LOAD httpfs;" succeeds even under --read-only, after which read_json() / read_csv() / read_text() / read_parquet() / ATTACH over an http(s) URL make outbound requests FROM the server host. A prompt-injected or misbehaving LLM agent can reach cloud metadata services (169.254.169.254 -> AWS/GCP/Azure credential theft), loopback admin services, and other hosts on the server private network.
DISCRIMINATOR (FP-control): a remote-fetch function is matched ONLY in combination with an INTERNAL / metadata target (169.254.169.254, link-local 169.254/16, metadata.google / metadata.azure, 127.0.0.1 / localhost / [::1] / 0.0.0.0, RFC1918 10.0.0.0/8 + 192.168.0.0/16, *.internal). Legitimate ETL pulls PUBLIC https data, not internal/metadata endpoints, so this combination is high-fidelity -- a naive "LOAD httpfs" or read_json("http...") match alone would be an FP-storm.
NOTE: RFC1918 172.16.0.0/12 (172.16-172.31) is omitted from the literal list to avoid loose-substring false matches; add the specific 172.16.-172.31. prefixes in environments that use that range.
ENCODED TARGETS: selection_internal_target_encoded also catches loopback/metadata written in decimal (2130706433 / 2852039166), hex (0x7f000001 / 0xa9fea9fe), octal (0177. / 0251.0376) and IPv6 short forms ([::], [::ffff:...]) -- standard SSRF filter-bypass encodings that evade a literal dotted-quad allow/deny list. These are paired with a remote-fetch function, so they stay high-fidelity (a benign fetch URL does not contain the decimal/hex form of a loopback or metadata address).
Generalises to the MCP DB-server class (motherduck / dbhub / any DuckDB or SQL-passthrough MCP DB server). OWASP LLM Top 10 2025: LLM06 (Excessive Agency).
TELEMETRY PREREQUISITE: requires the executed SQL string to be logged -- by the MCP server (query / audit log) or a body-logging reverse proxy / WAF (the JSON-RPC tools/call "sql" argument). Map that field to QueryText below. Most default deployments do NOT log executed SQL -> prerequisite-gated detection, NOT universal coverage.
